sections.heading: Styx stands with Zeus
sections.translation:
Styx, Oceanus’s daughter, joined in love with Pallas
and in their halls gave birth to Zelos and Nike with her lovely ankles.
She also bore Kratos and Bia, her glorious children.
They have no home, no seat away from Zeus,
and take no road unless the god leads them.
They always sit beside Zeus, whose thunder crashes loud.

This was what deathless Styx, Oceanus’s daughter, had planned
on the day when Zeus, the lightning-flinger of Olympus,
called all the immortal gods to high Olympus.
He said that any god who fought beside him against the Titans
would lose none of their privileges:
each would keep the honor they had held among the immortal gods.
And anyone left without honor or privilege under Cronus
would receive both, as was their right.

Deathless Styx was the first to come to Olympus,
bringing her children, following her dear father’s advice.
Zeus honored her and gave her special gifts.
He made her the great oath by which the gods swear,
and gave her children a home beside him for all time.
He fulfilled his promises to all the gods, every one.
He himself holds mighty power and rules.
sections.summary: Styx and her children support Zeus. He rewards them and keeps his promises to the other gods.

cards.label: Styx
cards.general: A goddess and a river whose water makes the gods’ most binding oath.
cards.here: She brings her children to support Zeus.

cards.label: Oceanus
cards.general: The god of the great river believed to circle the world.
cards.here: Styx’s father, who advises her to join Zeus.

cards.label: Pallas
cards.general: A god from the Titan family.
cards.here: The father of Styx’s four children.

cards.label: Zelos
cards.general: The spirit of rivalry and the drive to excel.
cards.here: One of Styx’s children, always beside Zeus.

cards.label: Nike
cards.general: The goddess of victory.
cards.here: One of Styx’s children, described as having lovely ankles.

cards.label: Kratos
cards.general: The spirit of power and might.
cards.here: One of Styx’s children, always beside Zeus.

cards.label: Bia
cards.general: The spirit of force.
cards.here: One of Styx’s children, always beside Zeus.

cards.label: Zeus
cards.general: The god of thunder and lightning, who becomes ruler of the gods.
cards.here: He promises rewards to the gods who fight beside him.

cards.label: Olympus
cards.general: The mountain home of the gods.
cards.here: Zeus gathers the gods there.

cards.label: Titans
cards.general: An older generation of gods.
cards.here: Zeus calls for allies to fight against them.

cards.label: Cronus
cards.general: Zeus’s father, who ruled the gods before him.
cards.here: Zeus offers honor to gods who had received none under Cronus.

cards.label: Honor and privileges
cards.general: A god’s recognized rank, rights, and share of power.
cards.here: Zeus promises to protect or grant these.

cards.label: Oath
cards.general: A solemn promise that binds the person making it.
cards.here: The gods swear their strongest oath by Styx.

sections.heading: Hecate’s family
sections.translation:
Phoebe came to Coeus’s bed, filled with love.
The goddess conceived in love with the god
and bore Leto in her dark-blue robe,
always gentle, kind to humans and immortal gods,
gentle from the very first, the kindest on Olympus.

Phoebe also bore renowned Asteria,
whom Perses once brought to his great house
to be called his dear wife.
Asteria conceived and gave birth to Hecate,
whom Zeus, Cronus’s son, honored above all others.
He gave her splendid gifts:
a share of the earth and the unharvested sea.
sections.summary: Phoebe has two daughters, Leto and Asteria. Asteria’s daughter Hecate receives great honors from Zeus.

cards.label: Phoebe
cards.general: A goddess of the older Titan generation.
cards.here: The mother of Leto and Asteria.

cards.label: Coeus
cards.general: A god of the older Titan generation.
cards.here: The father of Phoebe’s daughters.

cards.label: Leto
cards.general: A goddess, later the mother of Apollo and Artemis.
cards.here: Phoebe’s gentle daughter, dressed in dark blue.

cards.label: Asteria
cards.general: A goddess, the sister of Leto.
cards.here: Perses’s wife and Hecate’s mother.

cards.label: Perses
cards.general: A god from the Titan family.
cards.here: Asteria’s husband and Hecate’s father.

cards.label: Hecate
cards.general: A goddess with powers reaching across earth, sea, and heaven.
cards.here: Zeus grants her a share of earth and sea.

cards.label: Zeus
cards.general: The ruler of the gods and son of Cronus.
cards.here: He gives Hecate exceptional honor.

cards.label: Cronus
cards.general: Zeus’s father and the gods’ earlier ruler.
cards.here: He is named to identify Zeus’s family.

cards.label: Olympus
cards.general: The mountain home of the gods.
cards.here: Leto is called the kindest there.

cards.label: Unharvested sea
cards.general: A traditional poetic description of the sea, often understood as bearing no crops.
cards.here: The sea is one of the realms in which Hecate receives a share.

sections.heading: Hecate keeps her honors
sections.translation:
Hecate also has a share of honor in starry heaven,
and the immortal gods honor her greatly.
Even now, whenever someone on earth
seeks divine favor with fine offerings, as custom requires,
they call on Hecate.
Great honor comes easily to anyone
whose prayers the goddess welcomes with goodwill.
She gives them prosperity too, for she has the power.

Of all the gods born from Gaia and Uranus
who received a share of honor,
Hecate has a portion of every one’s share.
Zeus, Cronus’s son, neither forced her aside
nor took away anything she had received
among the Titans, the earlier gods.
She keeps her share from that first division.
Though an only child, the goddess has no smaller share
of honor and privilege on earth, in heaven, and at sea,
but far more still, because Zeus honors her.
sections.summary: Hecate keeps her ancient powers and honors. She can answer prayers and give people success and prosperity.

cards.label: Hecate
cards.general: A goddess whose powers extend across earth, sea, and heaven.
cards.here: She keeps her earlier rights and can grant blessings to people.

cards.label: Offerings
cards.general: Gifts or sacrifices presented to a god.
cards.here: People make them while asking for divine favor.

cards.label: Prosperity
cards.general: Wealth, success, and a flourishing life.
cards.here: A blessing Hecate has the power to give.

cards.label: Gaia
cards.general: Earth herself, understood as a goddess.
cards.here: With Uranus, she is the parent of the older gods.

cards.label: Uranus
cards.general: Sky himself, understood as a god.
cards.here: With Gaia, he is the parent of the older gods.

cards.label: Zeus
cards.general: The ruler of the gods.
cards.here: He protects Hecate’s earlier privileges and gives her great honor.

cards.label: Cronus
cards.general: Zeus’s father and the gods’ earlier ruler.
cards.here: Zeus is identified as his son.

cards.label: Titans
cards.general: The older generation of gods descended from Gaia and Uranus.
cards.here: Hecate already held privileges among them before Zeus ruled.

cards.label: Share of honor
cards.general: An allotted part of divine authority, rank, and privileges.
cards.here: Hecate shares in the powers assigned to the older gods.

uncertainties: At line 413, the traditional sea epithet translated as “unharvested” has an uncertain exact meaning; “barren” is another common rendering.
